To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

SML-2 is the first cysteine-rich lectin isolated from a protozoan, it is the first lectin from the PAN-module superfamily that has a lectin domain, and it is the first cystein-rich lectin that crystallized.

we isolated and characterized a novel cysteine-rich lectin from the parasite Sarcocysti s muris and that the crystals diffracting to high resolution at the synchrotron are suitable for X-ray structure determination.
a novel Sarcostis lectin was characterized and crystallized, and that it has potential for further structure-function studies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural characterization of SML-1 and SML-2 and with the elucidation of the carbohydrate-binding site.
the structural characterization of the novel SML-2 lectin from S. muris.

the isolation and characterization of a novel SML-2 lectin and with the crystallization of the lectin in complex with its carbohydrate ligand, which may serve as a model to understand the molecular basis of host-parasite interactions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this is the first report of a novel S. muris lectin (Sml-2) and that it is a member of the so-called PAN module superfamily of cysteine-rich proteins.
SML-2 is a novel member of the PAN-module superfamily of lectins.
SML-2 is the first member of the Sarcocystidae family to be characterized at the molecular level and to crystallize.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have successfully crystallized SML-2 and that we have obtained crystals of SML- 2 cocrystalling with Au galactoside.
SML-2 has the potential to serve as a template for the design of novel carbohydrate-binding proteins.
the crystallization of SML-1, SML-1/Au galactose and SML-2/Au galactosides was achieved.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SML-2 is a novel lectin with a PAN module and that the cocrystallization with Au galactoside results in a different crystal form.
the SML-2 crystal structure can be solved by molecular replacement using the SML-1 structure (PDB entry 2h4w) as the search model.
Sarcocystidae, a family of apicomplexa, are a rich source of novel proteins with potential for biotechnological and medical applications.
